summary: This Old House discusses installing and configuring a sub panel to serve a distant wing of a house (office, master suite, and garage mechanical space) when the main panel is remote. The video covers siting the sub panel in the proposed area near an open sectional wall, pouring a concrete slab and adding a 2x4 wall to mount the panel, and routing a single feeder cable into the sub panel rather than running many circuits. It then explains the relationship to the main service (initial 100 A panel in the main house), the plan to upgrade to a newer panel with arc-fault and GFCI protection, and the consideration of increasing service capacity from 100 A to 200 A or potentially 400 A based on load calculations that include heating/cooling, cooking, lighting, and future EV charging. The utility’s requirement to justify a 400 A service is highlighted, along with the practical steps of performing load calculations and the need to “homework” the sizing before upgrading.
